narrative.text:
I’ve read the rereview. I’ll address the five LOWs separately, check registration identity before changing hint cleanup, and run fresh base/head suites on both Node versions. The thread path remains explicitly incomplete under the programme’s engineering constraint.

The registration cleanup now uses the existing connection/transport-epoch pair captured at dispatch, plus the registered entry’s object identity. Tests cover replacement connections, same-object epoch changes, and conservative legacy calls. The destination-keyed diagnostic bound and expanded AST guard are also implemented; fresh suites and mutation checks are running.

A further binding clarification exposed one ambiguous case: a delayed public call carrying the same connection and epoch after re-registration has no old-entry token. I’ll make that guarded path refuse retirement and test it explicitly, rather than claim full generation safety. I’m stopping the two superseded head runs before this correction; the base runs continue.

All 16 final-head mutants built and were killed by assertions, including the old-transport epoch check and disconnect’s captured-pair check. Both fresh base suites ended with one timeout cancellation in unchanged `workspace-three-way.test.js` (0 failures, 63 skipped); I’m retaining those as failed gates, not passes. Final-head suites are still running.

Understood. I’ll report every run, use “cancellation reproduced on base, cause unknown/load-dependent” only if the comparisons support it, and keep the required lower-concurrency reruns and isolated-file checks sequential.

The first predeclared matched run is green: base on Node 22.23.3 has 9802 tests — 9739 pass, 0 fail, 63 skipped, 0 cancelled. The pinned head is now running at concurrency 8. The earlier parallel-run results remain separate; this does not establish their cancellation cause.
